headline: Bitcoin is holding just under $65,000 into Monday's European morning with fear still extreme, and the biggest bitcoin options bet is now protection against a fall below $60,000 ahead of Fed Chair Warsh's remarks at noon ET.

market.asOf: Read at about 08:01 UTC Mon 16 Nov (15:01 Bangkok) from CoinGecko's homepage table. The 24-hour direction could not be confirmed this run: CoinMarketCap's pages showed BTC down 2.73% and ETH down 6.05%, which CoinGecko did not match. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Extreme fear: CoinGecko's gauge read 19 out of 100 (Extreme Fear) at about 08:01 UTC; CoinMarketCap's index showed 12/100 at about 08:04 UTC; Alternative.me's index was 10 on Monday, against 29 a week ago, per Coin Gabbar.

stories.title: Bitcoin stuck near $65,000 as the biggest options bet becomes a fall below $60,000
stories.summary: Bitcoin has steadied after its weekend low near $62,000 but has not recovered, trading in a narrow range around $65,000 into Europe's morning. In bitcoin options, the most popular contract is now a bet that the price falls below $60,000, not one that it rises above $100,000. A renewed sell-off in AI-linked stocks hit Asian markets.
points: Bitcoin was up 0.6% at $64,866.50 and ether up about 1% at $1,817.23 at 05:25 GMT, per Investing.com.
The weekend low was $61,970.30 per The Crypto Basic and "as low as $62,000" per The Block; The Block put the weekly fall at 14.2% to $64,910.

On Deribit, the $60,000 put (a bet on a fall) has about $900M in open interest against about $867M for the $100,000 call, per CoinDesk, which said Paradigm saw over $1B of put block trades in two days.
Volmex's 30-day bitcoin implied-volatility index, a gauge of expected price swings, hit 57.13 on Sunday, its highest since June, before easing to 44, per CoinDesk.
Tech-heavy stock indexes in Japan, Korea and Taiwan fell, with Taiwan's Taiex down more than 4%, and Nasdaq 100 futures were down 0.5%, per Reuters.

sources.label: Reuters Morning Bid via Yahoo: Asian stocks

stories.title: Big week for interest rates: Warsh speaks today, December hike odds near 94%, ETFs after $1.91B of outflows
stories.summary: Fed Chair Warsh gives remarks at noon ET today, and futures traders see a December interest-rate rise as very likely; that is a market bet, not a Fed decision. US spot bitcoin ETFs reopen after seven straight days of withdrawals. Retail sales, Nvidia results, the Fed's minutes and Anthropic's share listing all land this week.
points: CME FedWatch showed a 94% chance of a 0.25-point hike in December and 6% for a 0.5-point move, per Investing.com; Reuters put the half-point odds at about 8%.
US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $1.91B over seven sessions through 13 November, per The Block; last week's outflow was $1.07B after $1.28B the week before, per FXStreet citing SoSoValue.
US ether ETFs lost $398.9M, their seventh straight week of withdrawals, per The Block.
Stablecoin supply fell about $17B over the month, per KuCoin's daily report citing Glassnode.
The Fed voted 10-2 in October to hold rates at 3.75-4.00%; minutes of that meeting are due Wednesday at 2pm ET, per crypto.news.

Reuters Morning Bid via Yahoo: half-point odds

stories.title: Binance aims to reopen all withdrawals this week after its $6.3B hack; CZ says it did not sell crypto
stories.summary: The world's largest crypto exchange is still restoring withdrawals after the 29 October hack, the largest crypto theft on record. Binance reopened 87 networks on 14 November and is targeting the rest by the end of this week; that is a target, not a guarantee. Founder CZ denied rumours that Binance sold crypto during the crash.
points: Binance reopened withdrawals for 87 networks on 14 November and aims to reopen all remaining networks and assets by the end of the following week, per PYMNTS.
The loss is put at $6.3B by PYMNTS and Bitcoin.com News, $6.34B by BigGo Finance; Binance says its reserves cover all losses, per PYMNTS.

Stolen assets included about 167,464 ETH and about $1.6B of USDT, and about $3B was frozen by third parties, per Bitcoin.com News; BigGo cites the AP at over $2.7B frozen and the FBI at over $1.2B seized.
CZ said "No, Binance did not sell crypto," and that he had been buying with stablecoins, per The Block.

briefs.title: Mining pool Luxor hit by an attack
briefs.summary: Mining power from over a dozen client accounts was redirected to another pool; Luxor patched the hole within 2 hours and will compensate clients, per The Block.

briefs.title: Kava Lend exploited
briefs.summary: About 55.2M KAVA (about $3.76M) was drained; about 49.2M was bridged out and most of it sold for about $2.09M, and KAVA fell about 39% to $0.042, per The Block.

briefs.title: Cardano holders reject a copper purchase
briefs.summary: A proposal to spend 22M ADA (about $5M) of treasury funds, about two-thirds of it on physical copper, was voted down 2.86B ADA against to about 20M ADA in favour, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: TRUMP memecoin falls below $1
briefs.summary: The TRUMP memecoin dropped below $1 for the first time since its 2025 launch, per Investing.com.
